title: Fairness Perceptions of Algorithmic Decision-Making: A Systematic Review of the Empirical Literature
reasoning: The paper is a systematic review of empirical literature regarding the perceived fairness of algorithmic decision-making (ADM). It evaluates these perceptions through the lens of moral and political philosophy (e.g., egalitarianism) and organizational justice (distributive, procedural, interactional, and informational fairness), which are core components of ethics in AI and automated systems.
